headline: Google has started rolling out its new Gemini 4 Argon model to paying subscribers and says it competes with the best AI models.
score_reason: Pool score 9 kept: a top lab's frontier model reaches paying users today; the benchmark claims are Google's own, and the viral floor of 7 is not touched.
importance_line: Paying Gemini users can now try Google's newest top model at a lower price than OpenAI and Anthropic charge, but the performance claims are Google's own, free and Plus users have no access date, and cheaper tokens may not mean cheaper tasks.
summary: The Verge reports that Google began rolling out Gemini 4 Argon on 13 Oct 2026 to Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app and in Search's AI mode, and to Ultra subscribers on its Antigravity development platform, after an earlier limited release to a small group of security specialists. Google says Argon beats OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 on tests of coding, security, science, finance and law, and has set an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens (tokens are small chunks of text), about a fifth of its rivals' flagship prices until the price doubles at the end of November.
notes: Read in full from the pool fulltext. What is new today is the rollout to paying users; Argon's restricted unveiling ran in our 1 Oct 2026 edition and its launch price on 9 Oct 2026, and the 2 Oct 2026 legal-benchmark item is an earlier fact, not repeated here as new. Viral floor 7 not lowered. Benchmark comparisons are Google's claims; no independent tests reported.
